candidacy.def: The fact or state of being a candidate standing for election to a public office (often confused with Spanish 'candidatura').
candidacy.quote: Diego (01:46): "I think, uh, the best option for my candidacy is to reduce poverty..."

quality-of-life.def: The standard of health, comfort, safety, and personal happiness experienced by an individual or society.
quality-of-life.quote: Diego (01:46): "I will invest in the quality of life of people... believe in new houses and gardens where everyone can walk calm."
quality-of-life.l1: calidad de vida y bienestar ciudadano

poverty.def: The state of being extremely poor and lacking sufficient money or resources to provide basic life necessities.
poverty.quote: Louie (02:57): "The poverty." / Diego (03:01): "The poverty... maybe in a short time we can increase salaries."

pledges.def: Solemn promises or formal commitments made by politicians during an election campaign.
pledges.quote: Louie (03:12): "What are your pledges? What do you pledge to do? Your promises?"

mandate.def: The official authority given to an elected official or government by voters to carry out specific policies.
mandate.quote: Louie (03:12): "To summarize, what are your... not mandate, what are your pledges?"
mandate.l1: mandato popular / autoridad conferida por los votantes

borders.def: The geographic line or boundary dividing two political states, regions, or sovereign countries.
borders.quote: Diego (03:46): "And not to close the borders of the countries, like in Spain."

diluting.def: Metaphorically reducing the strength, value, or financial power of a commitment, fund, or legal guarantee.
diluting.quote: Louie (06:38): "Today, they started diluting it... diluting is when you add more water to sugar and make it weaker."
diluting.l1: diluir / recortar el poder adquisitivo progresivamente

triple-lock.def: A British political commitment ensuring the state pension rises annually by the highest of: inflation, wage growth, or 2.5%.
triple-lock.quote: Louie (07:23): "We have something called the Triple Lock Pension. It raises every year at the same rate as inflation or average wage."
triple-lock.l1: triple blindaje de pensiones (fórmula de revalorización en el Reino Unido)

inflation.def: A general, sustained increase in the prices of goods and services over time, reducing purchasing power.
inflation.quote: Louie (08:28): "Every year our pensions get stronger... at the same rate as inflation."
inflation.l1: inflación (aumento sostenido del coste de vida)

average-wage.def: The mean statistical earnings paid to employees across the economy during a specific financial period.
average-wage.quote: Louie (08:41): "Or the average wage... wage, so like salary, okay?"
average-wage.l1: salario medio / sueldo promedio de los trabajadores

wage.def: A fixed regular payment earned for work or services, typically calculated by the hour, week, or month.
wage.quote: Diego (09:00): "Wage, wage is like salary, no?" / Louie (09:02): "Yeah, yeah, exactly."
wage.l1: salario / sueldo (confundido fonéticamente por el note-taker con 'weight')

interest-rates.def: The proportion of a loan charged as interest to the borrower, typically expressed as an annual percentage.
interest-rates.quote: Louie (09:02): "Interest rates... so in England you can't get poor as an old person."
interest-rates.l1: tipos de interés bancarios / tasas de interés

afford.def: To have enough money, fiscal headroom, or resources to pay for a service or social entitlement.
afford.quote: Louie (09:36): "And it sounds good. However, we can't afford it."
afford.l1: permitirse económicamente / asumir el coste financiero

pensioners.def: People who receive a pension, especially retired individuals who have stopped working.
pensioners.quote: Louie (10:06): "So pensioners get too much benefit... and we have three pensions: state, union, and work."

state-pension.def: A regular government payment made to retired citizens who have reached statutory pension age.
state-pension.quote: Louie (07:57): "In England, we have the state pension." / Diego (08:03): "That's like in Spain."

union-pension.def: A supplemental occupational pension fund managed by a trade union or professional guild.
union-pension.quote: Louie (11:07): "I have a union pension as well, from when I was working in London."

employer.def: A person or organization that employs people and pays their wages and occupational benefits.
employer.quote: Louie (10:44): "You and your employer have to have a work pension..."

transfer.def: To pass ownership or legal entitlement of money or pension assets from one person or account to another.
transfer.quote: Louie (15:19): "You can't transfer your state pension... say you die, your children do not get it."
transfer.l1: traspasar / legar en herencia derechos económicos

401k.def: An American employer-sponsored, tax-advantaged defined-contribution retirement account.
401k.quote: Louie (16:05): "Is it a 401(k)? In America you can pay into a 401(k) and your company will match it."
401k.l1: plan de pensiones privado 401(k) estadounidense con aportación empresarial

match-funds.def: To provide an equal financial contribution matching the amount an employee saves into a fund.
match-funds.quote: Louie (16:27): "In America you can pay into a 401(k) and your company will match it."
match-funds.l1: equiparar / aportar la misma cuantía que el trabajador

retirement-age.def: The action, period, or fact of leaving one's job and ceasing to work permanently.
retirement-age.quote: Louie (17:28): "When is retirement? When do you retire?" / Diego (17:33): "It is about 65 more or less."

relatives.def: The members of a person's extended family connected by blood or marriage.
relatives.quote: Louie (18:15): "In my relatives, they don't die... my grandparents are all coming up to 100 years old."

won-the-lottery.def: To suddenly come into vast, life-altering wealth through fortune or windfall.
won-the-lottery.quote: Louie (19:22): "We say in England: if you won the lottery, for sure... I would live on the North Pole away from everyone."
won-the-lottery.l1: ganar la lotería / tocarte el premio gordo

sociable.def: Willing to talk and engage with other people in an outgoing, friendly manner.
sociable.quote: Louie (19:56): "I'm a very sociable person, but I'm not really... I like to be alone."

older-brother.def: Taking on the psychological archetype of the responsible, protective guide who resolves others' dilemmas.
older-brother.quote: Louie (20:16): "Wherever I go, I become the older brother, always. People are calling me every day asking what do you think."
older-brother.l1: hermano mayor (arquetipo de liderazgo y protección familiar)

two-truths-and-a-lie.def: A classic deductive party and classroom icebreaker where a speaker states three claims, one of which is false.
two-truths-and-a-lie.quote: Louie (20:49): "We're gonna play a different game now: it's called two truths and a lie."
two-truths-and-a-lie.l1: dos verdades y una mentira (juego de deducción y oratoria)

paper-planes.def: The globally celebrated 2007 alternative hip-hop single by British-Sri Lankan artist M.I.A.
paper-planes.quote: Louie (22:17): "Do you know the singer M.I.A.? She sings a song called Paper Planes."

hates-my-guts.def: An informal English idiom meaning to feel intense, visceral dislike or animosity toward someone.
hates-my-guts.quote: Louie (23:05): "She absolutely hates my guts for a few reasons... in my previous job we operated high-end clubs."
hates-my-guts.l1: me odia con toda su alma / me detesta visceralmente

invite-only.def: An exclusive event or venue admission policy restricted strictly to individuals with formal invitations.
invite-only.quote: Louie (23:25): "I used to say to her: I'm sorry, you can't come in. We're full and it's by invite only."
invite-only.l1: exclusivo por invitación / de acceso restringido

californication.def: The multi-platinum 1999 album and Grammy-winning title track by the American rock band Red Hot Chili Peppers.
californication.quote: Louie (24:50): "They're a famous band... they sing Californication or something (note-taker: California Cation)."
californication.l1: Californication (disco icónico de Red Hot Chili Peppers)

musically-inclined.def: Having a natural talent, deep interest, or perceptive ear for music and melody.
musically-inclined.quote: Louie (27:20): "And the Red Hot Chili Peppers... I'm not very musically inclined."
musically-inclined.l1: con vocación o inclinación musical innata

donated.def: Gave money, goods, or personal items to an organization or charity to help a cause without seeking profit.
donated.quote: Louie (27:26): "They donated their skateboard to charity... they came in to see their skateboards years later."

arena.def: London's famous 20,000-capacity entertainment dome located on the Greenwich Peninsula.
arena.quote: Louie (25:45): "At the O2 Arena in London... a big, huge event space that hosts world tennis and concerts."
arena.l1: el O2 Arena de Londres (icónico estadio cubierto)

event-space.def: A large specialized commercial or cultural hall designed to host live performances, galas, and sports.
event-space.quote: Louie (25:49): "The O2 Arena is like a big, huge event space and it has world tennis and gigs."

wallpaper.def: The digital background image displayed on a computer screen, smartphone, or tablet desktop.
wallpaper.quote: Diego (29:12): "I don't know, but my wallpaper is Messi."
wallpaper.l1: fondo de pantalla del ordenador o móvil

messi.def: The iconic Argentine forward considered one of the greatest football players in world history.
messi.quote: Diego (29:03): "I have a signed T-shirt of Messi... my wallpaper is Messi."
messi.l1: Leo Messi (confundido por el note-taker con 'messy')

deputy-assistant.def: The chief deputy, executive assistant, or closest advisor who operates directly beneath the leader.
deputy-assistant.quote: Diego (30:04): "One of them told me that he was the assistant of the President of Spain (note-taker: second half)."
deputy-assistant.l1: segundo al mando / asesor personal de Presidencia

reggaeton.def: A musical genre originating in Puerto Rico blending reggae rhythms, hip hop, and Latin vocal cadences.
reggaeton.quote: Diego (31:22): "We were watching famous artists of reggaeton... and in my DJ sets I play reggaeton and electronic."

vip-stage.def: An exclusive backstage or reserved platform giving special access to performers and celebrities.
vip-stage.quote: Diego (31:22): "We were in the VIP stage... later in the front stage we were talking with him."
vip-stage.l1: zona VIP / palco reservado para invitados especiales

signed-jersey.def: An authentic sports jersey bearing the handwritten personal autograph of an elite athlete.
signed-jersey.quote: Louie (34:47): "How did you get Messi's signed Messi shirt?" / Diego (35:02): "My aunt knows people on the staff of FC Barcelona."

hanging-on-wall.def: Suspended or mounted vertically on a wall for display rather than stored in a wardrobe.
hanging-on-wall.quote: Diego (36:06): "It is hanging on the wall... I've never put it on, I have it hanging on the wall."
hanging-on-wall.l1: colgado en la pared como pieza de exposición

purpose-of-art.def: The philosophical rationale behind artistic creation: to stimulate emotion, reflect reality, and reveal unseen dimensions.
purpose-of-art.quote: Louie (37:36): "What is the purpose of art in society?" / Diego (37:49): "To see things that in real life you can't see."
purpose-of-art.l1: el propósito y función social del arte

inspire.def: To fill someone with the urge, courage, or mental stimulation to feel or do something creative.
inspire.quote: Louie (38:04): "Can't see... maybe to inspire? Or to reflect? Reflect things in real life."

reflect.def: To mirror, represent, or communicate the conditions and truths of human existence through creative medium.
reflect.quote: Diego (38:16): "Yes, reflect things in real life that you can't see."
reflect.l1: reflejar la realidad profunda y el sentir humano

design.def: The deliberate aesthetic and functional plan of a building, object, or visual work (misheard as 'Giselle').
design.quote: Diego (38:33): "Maybe design / architecture... to see amazing buildings."

architecture.def: The art, discipline, and science of designing and constructing complex buildings and physical structures.
architecture.quote: Louie (38:45): "Architecture... to see amazing buildings. Good, good."

wisdom.def: The quality of having experience, good judgment, and deep practical insight into human life.
wisdom.quote: Louie (38:48): "What is the difference between knowledge and wisdom? Wisdom is when you learn from experience..."
wisdom.l1: sabiduría práctica destilada de la experiencia

knowledge.def: Facts, theoretical information, and skills acquired through education, reading, or conceptual study.
knowledge.quote: Louie (38:48): "Knowledge is you can read and understand, but you haven't lived it."
knowledge.l1: conocimiento teórico adquirido por el estudio

lived-it.def: Having personally experienced the challenges, hardships, or realities of an endeavor firsthand.
lived-it.quote: Louie (39:06): "Knowledge you can read and understand, but wisdom means you have lived it."

attachment.def: An emotional dependency or bond to a person, role, or outcome, often rooted in habitual security.
attachment.quote: Louie (39:37): "What is the difference between love and attachment? Attachment is when you are depending on them."

lust.def: Intense sexual or physical attraction that lacks emotional depth, unconditional concern, or spiritual devotion.
lust.quote: Louie (40:33): "Lust. L-U-S-T. It's when it's not really love; you are attracted to them, but it's superficial."
lust.l1: lujuria / atracción puramente física y superficial

superficial.def: Existing or occurring only at the surface level; lacking depth of character, feeling, or understanding.
superficial.quote: Louie (40:33): "It's when you are more attracted to them, but it is superficial..."

inquisitive.def: Having or showing an eager, insatiable desire to know and investigate everything; intensely curious.
inquisitive.quote: Louie (41:40): "Beyond my job I think I'm inquisitive... inquisitive is like very curious, I always want to know."
inquisitive.l1: inquisitivo / de curiosidad incansable por aprender

motivation.def: The internal drive, desire, or psychological energy that causes someone to act and maintain effort.
motivation.quote: Diego (43:08): "Motivation in learning... because I'm always trying to improve myself, I always have new goals."

achievements.def: Things done successfully with effort, skill, or courage; milestones reached.
achievements.quote: Diego (43:35): "I have always new achievements or goals... and try to achieve my milestones abroad."

contentment.def: A peaceful state of psychological satisfaction and happiness with what one currently possesses.
contentment.quote: Louie (43:53): "How do you balance ambition and contentment? Contentment is when you are happy with your situation."
contentment.l1: contentamiento / serenidad y paz con lo presente

content.def: In a state of peaceful satisfaction and acceptance with the current state of affairs.
content.quote: Diego (44:13): "Content... it's the first time I see that word." / Louie (44:14): "Content is: are you happy?"
content.l1: satisfecho / en paz con las circunstancias presentes

thief-of-joy.def: A famous aphorism ('Comparison is the thief of joy') warning that measuring oneself against others destroys happiness.
thief-of-joy.quote: Louie (48:41): "Comparison is the thief of joy... people compare themselves to realities that aren't even real."
thief-of-joy.l1: el ladrón de la alegría (la comparación destructiva de la felicidad)

live-abroad.def: To reside in a foreign country outside one's homeland for work or study.
live-abroad.quote: Diego (49:45): "For me trying to live abroad outside my city will be a success... you earn so much experience."
live-abroad.l1: vivir en el extranjero / residir fuera de España

stronger-cv.def: A curriculum vitae featuring superior international experience, multilingual skills, and advanced competence.
stronger-cv.quote: Diego (51:00): "If later I come back, I know that I have a much stronger CV than the others."
stronger-cv.l1: currículum vítae mucho más potente y competitivo

work-abroad.def: To practice one's profession in an international market or corporate environment.
work-abroad.quote: Louie (50:20): "When you live and work in another country in the same field, you become so much better."
work-abroad.l1: trabajar en el extranjero en el mismo sector profesional

redundant.def: Dismissed from employment because one's job position is no longer needed by the company (downsized).
redundant.quote: Louie (52:20): "She had done the same job for years, and she has been made redundant."
redundant.l1: despedido por amortización del puesto / regulación de empleo

nepotism.def: The practice among those with power or influence of favoring relatives or friends, especially by giving them jobs.
nepotism.quote: Louie (52:37): "My brother worked in our company... because nepotism, right? Get him trained and then come over."
nepotism.l1: nepotismo / favoritismo hacia familiares en el trabajo

accomplishment.def: Something that has been achieved successfully through sustained effort, technical skill, and discipline.
accomplishment.quote: Louie (53:34): "What accomplishment are you most proud of?" / Diego (54:30): "I study everything before I implement it."

delusional.def: Characterized by idiosyncratic beliefs or unshakeable ambitions that skeptics deem irrational or impossible.
delusional.quote: Louie (55:37): "I am very proud in building things that people thought would never be, and being delusional!"
delusional.l1: delirantemente audaz / convencido frente a todo pronóstico

cockroaches.def: A scavenging beetle-like insect with long antennae, commonly found in domestic habitats and tropical climates.
cockroaches.quote: Diego (57:35): "What thing said, croc. Riches? Cucaraches." / Louie (58:03): "Cockroaches."

scorpions.def: A predatory arachnid with pincers and a venomous curved tail sting, common in tropical jungle climates.
scorpions.quote: Louie (58:46): "Bats, snakes, cockroaches, huge spiders, scorpions... crazy, but it was an adventure."

shed-skin.def: The biological process (ecdysis) where reptiles cast off their outer dead epidermis as they grow.
shed-skin.quote: Louie (59:07): "A snake came into my room, and it shed its skin and left!"
shed-skin.l1: mudar de piel (proceso natural de los reptiles)

tet.def: Tết Nguyên Đán, the most sacred and important celebration of the Vietnamese Lunar New Year.
tet.quote: Louie (01:00:25): "Do you know about Chinese New Year? Tet, right? We have Tet here in Vietnam."

pseudoscience.def: A collection of beliefs or practices mistakenly regarded as being based on scientific method (e.g. astrology).
pseudoscience.quote: Louie (01:00:25): "It's deeply pseudo. Science, right? But they believe in it... the Year of the Snake."
pseudoscience.l1: pseudociencia / creencias sin base científica empírica

rice-fields.def: Flooded parcels of arable land used for growing semi-aquatic paddy rice in Southeast Asia.
rice-fields.quote: Louie (01:01:17): "They have rice fields, right? And when it floods, all the snakes leave the rice fields."

dodging.def: To avoid someone or something by a sudden, quick agile movement aside.
dodging.quote: Louie (01:01:27): "You're driving your motorbike and you're just trying to dodge snakes... hundreds of them."

democracy.def: A system of government by the whole population, typically through elected representative officials.
democracy.quote: Louie (01:02:29): "Is democracy the best form of government?" / Diego (01:02:40): "Depends on the country."

corrupt.def: Having or showing a willingness to act dishonestly in return for money, power, or personal gain.
corrupt.quote: Diego (01:03:13): "It's a good thing if it is well done." / Louie (01:03:22): "Yeah, if it's not corrupt."
corrupt.l1: corrupto / viciado por sobornos e intereses deshonestos
